result.markdown:
# How to pass Wise Business address verification for a newly registered UK company

If you've just incorporated a UK limited company through Companies House, the main challenge with Wise Business verification is proving that your company has a **genuine, verifiable business operating address**, rather than simply showing that the company legally exists.

The important distinction is that Wise may ask you to verify two different things\:

1. **Registered business address** – the official address recorded at Companies House.
2. **Trading or operating address** – where your business actually operates or is managed.

These addresses can be different, but you need to provide the correct evidence for the address Wise is asking you to verify.

## 1\. Which documents actually work?

According to Wise's official [business address verification requirements](https://wise.com/help/articles/2969315/how-does-wise-verify-my-business-address), these are the main acceptable options.

| Document | Wise's requirements |
|--------|--------|
| Electricity or gas bill | Issued within 3 months |
| Broadband or landline bill | Issued within 3 months |
| Business bank statement | Issued within 3 months |
| Personal bank statement | Can work for a significant company owner/director |
| Council tax bill | Official council document |
| Signed tenancy agreement | Current and signed by both parties |
| Business insurance | Policy showing the relevant address |
| HMRC correspondence | Official tax documentation |


For a newly incorporated company, there is an especially useful provision\:

**If you work from home and don't have bills in your company's name, Wise can accept personal documents in the name of a significant owner or director of the registered company.**

The personal document must show the same address you've entered as your company's trading address.

Source: [Wise – How does Wise verify my business address?](https://wise.com/help/articles/2969315/how-does-wise-verify-my-business-address?utm_source=chatgpt.com)\.

## 2\. The biggest problem: virtual registered office addresses

(Important)

Suppose your company was incorporated using an address from\:

- 1st Formations
- Companies Made Simple
- Rapid Formations
- Your accountant
- A virtual office provider

That address can legitimately be your registered office at Companies House.

However, Wise explicitly says that your trading address cannot be\:

- A virtual office.
- A mail forwarding service.
- A PO Box.
- A company formation agent's address.
- A solicitor's office.

This is where many newly incorporated companies encounter problems.

**The solution\:** Keep your registered office address as it appears on Companies House, but provide your genuine physical working address as your trading address.

Wise allows these addresses to be different. [wise.com](https://wise.com/help/articles/2969315/how-does-wise-verify-my-business-address?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[wise.com](https://wise.com/help/articles/ixgxNfPDKgxCHQU2XfuyY/getting-your-business-verified-in-the-uk-and-eea/hjQb2P34NT.midi?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[wise.com](https://wise.com/gb/blog/how-to-get-limited-company-verified-using-wise-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[wise.com](https://wise.com/help/articles/2769792/how-can-i-verify-my-business?origin=related-article-2977981&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 3\. Best approach for a newly registered UK Ltd

Here is the practical approach I would recommend\:

1. **Keep the Companies House registered address**
   
   Enter the exact address shown on your incorporation records.
2. **Use your actual working address as the trading address**
   
   If you run the company from home, use your genuine home working address.
3. **Prepare personal address evidence**
   
   If you're a director or significant owner, prepare a recent personal bank statement, utility bill or council tax bill showing that address.
4. **Prepare company registration evidence**
   
   Have your Certificate of Incorporation and Companies House company number available.
5. **Submit only through Wise's verification request**
   
   Upload a clear, complete PDF or image. Ensure the name and address match the information supplied to Wise.

Wise also says business registration documents, bank statements and utility bills should generally be less than three months old. [wise.com](https://wise.com/help/articles/2969315/how-does-wise-verify-my-business-address?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[wise.com](https://wise.com/help/articles/2769792/how-can-i-verify-my-business?origin=related-article-2977981&utm_source=chatgpt.com)[wise.com](https://wise.com/help/articles/ixgxNfPDKgxCHQU2XfuyY/getting-your-business-verified-in-the-uk-and-eea/hjQb2P34NT.midi?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 4\. What if your company has just been incorporated and has no bills yet?

This is perfectly normal.

You don't necessarily need to wait three months or establish a long business history.

For example, if\:

- Your UK Ltd was incorporated recently.
- You're the sole director and shareholder.
- You haven't opened a business bank account.
- You don't have business utility bills.
- You haven't started generating revenue.

You can still apply. Wise's UK verification process considers the company registration, directors, owners, business activities and trading address separately. [wise.com](https://wise.com/help/articles/ixgxNfPDKgxCHQU2XfuyY/getting-your-business-verified-in-the-uk-and-eea/hjQb2P34NT.midi?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[wise.com](https://wise.com/gb/blog/how-to-get-limited-company-verified-using-wise-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Don't manufacture documents or use an address where you don't actually operate.

## 5\. What Wise checks beyond the address

Be prepared for additional verification questions, particularly for a new company\:

- What products or services does the company provide?
- Where will customers come from?
- Which countries will you send and receive payments from?
- What is your expected monthly transaction volume?
- What is the source of your initial business funds?
- Who owns 25% or more of the company?

Wise may also request director identification and ownership documentation. [wise.com](https://wise.com/help/articles/2969315/how-does-wise-verify-my-business-address?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[wise.com](https://wise.com/help/articles/2769792/how-can-i-verify-my-business?origin=related-article-2977981&utm_source=chatgpt.com)[wise.com](https://wise.com/help/articles/ixgxNfPDKgxCHQU2XfuyY/getting-your-business-verified-in-the-uk-and-eea/hjQb2P34NT.midi?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 6\. Let me assess your exact situation

There are a few different scenarios, and the best approach depends on how you incorporated your company and where you actually operate.
